run.question: In Loki, run the query `{service="checkout"}` against namespace app-282 and tell me how many error-level log lines come back. If the selector returns nothing, find the right one.

report.summary: The requested selector `{service="checkout"}` does not match the Loki label set used in namespace app-282: the streams there carry `acme_service`, `job`, `filename`, `level`, `namespace`, `pod` and `stream`, and the checkout logs are labelled `acme_service="checkout"`. Using the working selector, 4 error-level log lines (level="ERROR") were counted in the sampled hour ending 2026-11-23T19:12:53Z, and the same 4 ERROR lines appeared over a 24-hour window ending at that time; the stream's full set of 16 lines in the hour was 4 ERROR, 2 WARN and 10 INFO, all from pod checkout-698c8f5df-gpbdr. No root cause was investigated or established here: this Run answered a log-count question only.

claims.text: Loki streams returned for namespace app-282 carry the labels acme_service, job, filename, level, namespace, pod and stream; the checkout lines show acme_service="checkout", job="checkout-logs", filename="/var/log/checkout.log", pod="checkout-698c8f5df-gpbdr" and level in {INFO, WARN, ERROR}. No `service` label appears in any returned stream.
Counting error-level lines with sum(count_over_time({namespace="app-282", acme_service="checkout", level="ERROR"}[1h])) over 2026-11-23T18:12:53Z–2026-11-23T19:12:53Z returns the single value 4.

The same hour's lines for {namespace="app-282", acme_service="checkout"} split by level and pod as ERROR=4, WARN=2, INFO=10, all on pod checkout-698c8f5df-gpbdr, so the 4 ERROR lines are the entire error-level population of that stream in the hour, not a subset cut by a line limit.

Over the wider 24-hour window 2026-11-22T19:12:53Z–2026-11-23T19:12:53Z the counts are identical — ERROR=4, WARN=2, INFO=10 — so no additional ERROR lines from this stream fall in the preceding day of the authorized window.

The four error-level lines recorded at 2026-11-23T19:12:22Z from pod checkout-698c8f5df-gpbdr read: "Payment processor refused: invalid token (txn 9d1f)", "Inventory check timed out for SKU-77481", "Order persistence failed: deadlock on orders table" and "Webhook delivery exhausted retries for partner ACME".

The label the question used (`service`) is probably an application-level name that this Loki tenant indexes under `acme_service`; the ERROR count above therefore describes acme_service="checkout" and should be re-checked if a different label mapping is expected.

gaps: The exact selector `{service="checkout"}` was queried and returned 0 streams, and `{namespace="app-282", service="checkout"}` also returned 0 streams; both views are status no_data with citable_as_fact=false, so they show only that those queries matched nothing and do not prove a `service` label is absent from the tenant.
The label inventory was read from the labels of returned lines, not from a Loki label/value listing endpoint, so other label names on streams that were not returned remain unknown.
Only the hour 2026-11-23T18:12:53Z–19:12:53Z and the 24 hours ending 2026-11-23T19:12:53Z were counted; error-line volume earlier in the authorized month (from 2026-10-24T19:12:53Z) was not checked.
Whether these four ERROR lines indicate a real checkout outage, and their downstream customer impact, was not investigated in this Run.
next_steps: Confirm the tenant's canonical service label (acme_service vs. a renamed `service`) against the Loki label API before reusing `{service="checkout"}` in dashboards or alerts.
If an incident view is needed, extend the ERROR count over the full authorized window and correlate it with checkout spans and Prometheus error-rate series.
